articles.title: Empirical Evaluation of Task-Based Permission Scoping Architecture for AI Agents
articles.summary: The paper evaluates a task-based permission scoping architecture for AI agents, addressing the risk that enterprise agents often carry broad static credentials unrelated to their current task. Using a fine-tuned RoBERTa-large security gate, the study reports classification performance comparable to Claude Haiku 4.5 and estimates that task-level permission controls could eliminate a large share of severity-weighted attack surface in agentic deployments.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is an early technical signal that enterprise AI adoption may require new security architectures beyond traditional role-based access control. While not directly investable, it highlights governance and identity-management bottlenecks that could influence enterprise agent deployment timelines and create demand for AI security, access-control, and workflow oversight solutions.
